key_insight: Wall curvature reshapes supersonic boundary-layer turbulence: concave walls promote structured triadic energy transfer and vortex breakdown, while convex walls suppress redistribution and retain energy in elongated streamwise streaks.
engineering_relevance: Distinguishing nonlinear scale selection from linear flow receptivity can inform turbulence modeling and flow-control strategies for curved supersonic surfaces.
method: Direct numerical simulations over continuously concave and convex walls.
Scale-resolved TKE budgets, triadic-transfer bispectra, and spectral proper orthogonal decomposition.
Global resolvent analysis to identify linear amplification and coherent-structure topology.
evidence_signal: DNS-based diagnostics reveal a low-spanwise-wavenumber outer-layer production peak over concave walls and suppressed pressure-strain redistribution over convex walls.
watch_item: The abstract provides no parameter ranges or quantitative validation metrics, limiting assessment of generalization to other Mach numbers, Reynolds numbers, and curvature profiles.
paper_title: Triadic energy cascades and linear amplification mechanisms in supersonic turbulent boundary layers over curved walls
